assessment.nobel_worthiness: Induced degradation of target proteins via E3 ligase recruitment is a new chemical modality: PROTACs turn a small molecule into a catalytic degrader, and the molecular-glue mechanism of thalidomide-class drugs (cereblon) explains a long-standing pharmacological puzzle. It reaches the ubiquitin-proteasome biochemistry and cancer/genome-stability questions I know well, and clinical degraders are in trials.
assessment.attribution: Crews and Deshaies founded and developed the PROTAC concept; Handa and Ito identified cereblon as the thalidomide target. Gray, Ciulli, Sakamoto and others made major contributions, so a three-person cap forces a hard choice; Crews, Deshaies and Handa best span concept and mechanism.
assessment.maturity: Strong independent confirmation across many labs and the first clinical data, but approved degrader drugs are still lacking, so recognition could be seen as slightly early.
uncertainties: Whether the committee would prefer to wait for an approved PROTAC drug.
Division between PROTAC pioneers and the cereblon/molecular-glue discoverers is unresolved.
Names such as Ciulli and Gray are left out by the three-person limit.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Phosphoramidite solid-phase synthesis made routine, automated, high-fidelity synthesis of oligonucleotides possible. It underlies PCR primers, sequencing, gene synthesis, CRISPR guides and oligonucleotide therapeutics. The discovery is clear, original and has had enormous lasting impact; the nucleic-acid chemistry is fundamental to my own field.
assessment.attribution: Caruthers developed the phosphoramidite method and automated synthesis; Hood's role was largely instrumentation/commercialisation of the synthesiser, so a single laureate is the cleanest configuration. This is my own reading of historical credit and I have not verified it independently.
assessment.maturity: Decades of universal use; if anything the recognition is overdue and the age of the key inventor is a timing risk.
uncertainties: Whether Hood or others deserve a share is uncertain.
Prior H-phosphonate and phosphotriester work (Letsinger, Khorana) could complicate priority.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Base editors use engineered deaminases to change single nucleotides without double-strand breaks. This is an elegant chemical solution to the genome-stability problem of repair-dependent editing, with clear therapeutic potential and rapid adoption. Its significance for DNA chemistry and mutagenesis is high.
assessment.attribution: David R. Liu led the concept and development; Komor and Gaudelli were the lead postdoctoral inventors of cytosine and adenine base editors. A fair configuration is Liu alone or Liu with the two first authors; Kondo and Nishida's deaminase-fusion work is a competing precedent.
assessment.maturity: Independent replication is broad and first clinical trials are reporting, but long-term safety and off-target (including RNA and bystander edits) data are still maturing. The prize may be better combined with prime editing in the same year.
uncertainties: Overlap with candidate B062 (prime editing) from the same lead laboratory.
Priority claims of Kondo and Nishida (Target-AID).

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Orthogonal tRNA/synthetase pairs for incorporating unnatural amino acids in living cells rewired the genetic code and gave chemists a way to place novel chemistry in proteins at defined sites. It has changed protein engineering and chemical biology and is conceptually clear and original.
assessment.attribution: Schultz established the in vivo approach and first unnatural amino acid incorporation in E. coli and yeast; Chin extended it to multicellular animals and quadruplet/ribosome-orthogonal systems; Wang's early work with Schultz was decisive. Yokoyama and Mehl also contributed. Schultz and Chin are the clearest core.
assessment.maturity: Mature with two decades of use, many applications and a robust body of independent confirmation, though no killer therapeutic application yet.
uncertainties: Dividing credit among Schultz, Chin, Wang, Yokoyama and Mehl is difficult.
Relative weight of the conceptual versus extension work is unclear.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Mass-spectrometry proteomics (shotgun, quantitative and targeted) made it possible to measure thousands of proteins and their modifications in cells and tissues. It is transformational for biochemistry, drug-target work and clinical biology.
assessment.attribution: Mann, Aebersold and Yates each led different, decisive strands: high-resolution quantitative MS, targeted/isotope-coded approaches, and shotgun database searching. Hunt and Gygi are also major contributors, so a three-person cap is restrictive. The ionization methods were already recognised in 2002, which helps focus this on the proteomic workflow.
assessment.maturity: Very mature and widely confirmed, though the field is a collection of methods, which makes a single sharp discovery statement hard.
uncertainties: Whether the committee views this as too diffuse for a prize.
Overlap with B049 and B029 (native MS, Orbitrap).

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Ionizable lipid nanoparticles are the enabling chemistry behind siRNA and mRNA medicines, including the COVID-19 vaccines. Their design solved the problem of nucleic-acid delivery and endosomal escape. Their impact on nucleic-acid medicine is large and clearly demonstrable.
assessment.attribution: Cullis's group developed the lipid nanoparticle formulation principles, with Hope, Madden and MacLachlan central to the work; Anderson and Langer contributed combinatorial lipid discovery. Allocation is unclear.
assessment.maturity: Clinically validated at scale, though the mRNA science was already recognised by the 2023 Medicine prize, so the chemistry-specific claim needs to be framed carefully.
uncertainties: Attribution within the Vancouver group and between Cullis and Anderson/Langer is contested.
Overlap with the earlier mRNA prize may reduce urgency.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Discovery that m6A is a reversible mRNA modification with writers, erasers and readers opened the field of epitranscriptomics. It links RNA chemistry to gene regulation and disease. The work is original and influential, though biological more than chemical in character.
assessment.attribution: He proposed reversible RNA methylation and identified FTO as a demethylase; Rechavi and Jaffrey independently mapped m6A transcriptome-wide in 2012. Jia, Dominissini and others are first-author contributors.
assessment.maturity: Broadly reproduced but the mapping methods and the functional interpretation of individual sites are still being refined.
uncertainties: Whether the committee sees this as chemistry or physiology/medicine.
Methodological controversies about m6A mapping and antibody specificity.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: In vitro selection of aptamers and ribozymes demonstrated that functional nucleic acids can be evolved from random libraries, linking nucleic-acid chemistry to molecular evolution and diagnostics/therapeutics (for example pegaptanib). Its importance is clear, though some of its conceptual territory has been covered by the 2018 evolution prize.
assessment.attribution: Gold and Tuerk (SELEX), Szostak and Ellington (aptamer terminology and selection), and Joyce (directed evolution of ribozymes) made near-simultaneous contributions; Szostak already has a Nobel. Priority is shared and a fair triple is hard to define.
assessment.maturity: Mature technology with continuing use, but impact in therapeutics has been modest.
uncertainties: Szostak is already a laureate (Medicine 2009), which may weigh against.
Simultaneous independent invention makes allocation contentious.
